posts.caption:
OILERS WIN 3-1. DRAISAITL SCORES TWICE, LEVI STOPS 28.

Leon Draisaitl scored twice and Devon Levi turned aside 28 of 29 shots as Edmonton beat the New York Rangers 3-1 tonight at Rogers Place.

Connor McDavid opened the scoring unassisted at 6:42 of the first, his 11th of the season. Draisaitl made it 2-0 at 2:59 of the second (Vasily Podkolzin, Mattias Ekholm), his 17th. Jaroslav Chmelar cut it to 2-1 with a shorthanded wrist shot at 5:05, assisted by Mika Zibanejad. Draisaitl sealed it with an unassisted, shorthanded empty-netter at 18:47 of the third, his 18th.

Levi, the first star, finished 28-for-29 (.966). He was perfect at even strength (18/18) and on the penalty kill (10/10). Dylan Garand stopped 17 of 19 in the loss.

The Rangers outshot Edmonton 29-20 and won 54% of the faceoffs. The Oilers led in hits 23-19 and blocks 11-7. Neither power play scored (New York 0-for-5, Edmonton 0-for-3). Edmonton has won both meetings this season, including a 4-1 win in New York on Nov. 1.

The Oilers are 13-3-3 (29 points), first in the Pacific, and have won two straight. They’re back at Rogers Place on Wednesday, Nov. 11, against the Philadelphia Flyers, with puck drop at 7 p.m. PT 6 p.m MT

posts.caption:
Gameday tomorrow: Rangers at Oilers
The Oilers are 12-3-3 with 27 points and sit 1st in the Pacific after Saturday’s 4-2 win over Vancouver. The Rangers are 10-7-1 with 21 points, 3rd in the Metro, and come into Rogers Place on a three-game win streak.
The special teams battle is a strength against a strength. Edmonton’s power play is clicking at 33.8% (22-for-65), and New York’s penalty kill is elite at 89.1% (49-for-55). The Oilers score 4.17 goals a game; the Rangers score 3.06 and allow 2.89.
McDavid has a point in all 18 games this season, with 10 goals and 37 assists for 47 points. Draisaitl is tied for the NHL goal lead with 16, and Bouchard has 31 points. For the Rangers, watch Fox (22 points), Lafrenière (18) and Zibanejad (15).
Dylan Garand will likely start in net for New York, since Shesterkin is out for the season with a lower-body injury. Edmonton hasn’t said whether Levi (7-1-0) or Jarry (4-1-3) gets the start.
Keep an eye on Nugent-Hopkins. He left Saturday’s game after taking a puck to the face and didn’t come back. Babcock doesn’t expect him to miss much time, but his status for Monday is still unclear.
The Oilers won the first meeting 4-1 at Madison Square Garden on Nov 1. Now it’s the rematch at Rogers Place.
Monday, Nov 9 · 7 PM MT | 6 PM PT · Rogers Place · SN+
#letsgooilers #oilcountry #rangers #copperandblue

posts.caption:
GAME DAY: Canucks @ Oilers 🛢️
Two straight losses (3-4 SO in New Jersey, 5-4 vs Anaheim). Time to get back on track. Edmonton (11-3-3) still sits 1st in the Pacific, and in comes Vancouver: 3-14-1, last in the league, four straight losses.
McDavid’s start is ridiculous: 44 points (10G-34A) in 17 games, with an assist in every one of them. Draisaitl has 14 goals, and Bouchard has 30 points from the back end.
Tale of the tape: the Oilers score 4.12 goals a game (most in the NHL) to Vancouver’s 2.94. The power play is cashing at 33.9% vs the Canucks’ 21.4%, and Vancouver gives up 4.61 a game.
What to watch: the crease. Andersen and Levi are on IR and Jarry is day-to-day with an illness, so Matt Tomkins is the projected starter against Leevi Meriläinen. Edmonton is 9-0-2 when it scores first, so a fast start matters. The last meeting was a 9-7 Oilers win in Vancouver on Oct 1.
Puck drop 8:00 PM PT at Rogers Place. Sportsnet.
#Oilers #LetsGoOilers #OilCountry #vanvsedm  Will the Oil get back in the win column?

posts.caption:
Day after at Rogers Place: Ducks 5, Oilers 4.
The good — McDavid’s four-point night (1G-3A), including a shorthanded goal, stretched his streak to 17. Edmonton owned the dot 34-18 and killed six of eight before the late push to one.
The bad — net-front losses and Tomkins’ .762 (16/21). Forty-six PIM and Podkolzin’s ejection stacked the deck. After leading 2-1, a second-period collapse left them chasing.
Babcock: “I thought our penalty kill was excellent (6-for-8). It really set us up to win the game… And then we didn’t look after it. They won both net fronts.”
Next: Canucks at Rogers Place, Sat Nov 7.
#Oilers #LetsGoOilers #OilCountry #ANAEDM

posts.caption:
5–4 DUCKS.
It was 1–1 after one on power-play goals from Cutter Gauthier and Evan Bouchard.
Connor McDavid put Edmonton in front shorthanded at 2:34 of the second, batting home his 10th of the season from Leon Draisaitl and Mattias Ekholm.
Pavel Mintyukov answered twice — at 3:37 from Beckett Sennecke and Drew Helleson, then at 6:15 from Judd Caulfield and Mikael Granlund — and Sennecke made it 4–2 with 38 seconds left in the period, from Tristan Luneau and Mintyukov.
Sennecke added a power-play goal at 1:42 of the third from Leo Carlsson and Gauthier to make it 5–2.
Kasperi Kapanen got one back on the power play at 16:24, a backhand from Ryan Nugent-Hopkins and McDavid, and Draisaitl scored with the extra attacker at 19:15 from McDavid and Bouchard to make it 5–4.
Mintyukov and Sennecke each finished with two goals and an assist. McDavid had a goal and three assists.
Shots: Oilers 27, Ducks 21. Tomkins 16/21 · Brossoit 23/27.
Final from Rogers Place.
#Oilers #LetsGoOilers #OilCountry #ANAEDM
